title: The Neuter Article Lo for Abstract Qualities

sections.content:
Spanish has no neuter nouns, but possesses the powerful neuter article **lo**. When combined with the masculine singular form of an adjective, it converts the adjective into an abstract noun meaning 'the [adjective] thing' or 'what is [adjective]':

• **lo bueno**: the good thing / what is good
• **lo malo**: the bad thing / the downside
• **lo importante**: the important thing / what matters
• **lo difícil**: the difficult part / what is hard
• **lo mejor / lo peor**: the best thing / the worst thing.

sections.title: Rules and Patterns
rows: the good thing / the bad thing

items.spanish: Lo importante es participar y aprender de los errores.
items.english: The important thing is to participate and learn from mistakes.

items.spanish: Lo bueno de vivir en el centro es que todo queda cerca.
items.english: The good thing about living downtown is that everything is close.

items.spanish: Lo difícil de este idioma son las conjugaciones verbales.
items.english: The difficult part of this language is the verb conjugations.

sections.content: *Lo* is NEVER used before nouns (never *lo libro*). Use *lo* ONLY with adjectives, adverbs, or past participles.
